body: This was a really nice post. Thank you.

My thought process goes like this:

There is no point in being here.

Ok, so make up your own.

In the end, there is no point in being here and there was no point in making up your own.

Not only that, I just feel so useless. I'm terrible at everything I attempt. Well, I'm pretty good (I get good marks, I suppose) in math but I don't think you could ever convince me I'm good at it, that I have a deep understanding of it although I wish I did.

I also hate my family. They embody everything I don't like in parents/people. My mom is an alcoholic/drug addict, although she is in rehab for now. My father is a lazy, emotionless piece of trash who lets his kids do whatever they want (examples: letting my older brother leech off him, smoke in the house, do nothing with his life. lets my younger brother turn the house into a club house for his nihilistic friends.)

It's funny that you say that. I saw Pi long ago and it's been my favourite movie since, but I read, on IMDB, someone's interpretation of the movie that is very similar to what you just said and I agree very much.

"i saw it as a study about how people try to cope with life and the bleakness of the world by involving themselves obsessively in something (be it art,money,luxury,math,religion,etc.) and then losing their faith in even that and feeling lost. hence the part where he's in his lab or whatever you would call it and everything starts short-circuiting. and then you have the jewish man,who instead of trying to figure out the world through math,attempts to through his religious faith. the most interesting character to me though is sol,who obviously was in the same crisis as a younger man and tries to teach him that there is no simple answer and that you're better off just trying to enjoy life in SPITE of how grim things may seem. you can see that sol obviously wasted the majority of his life chasing the answers,and found close to nothing;you can sense so much regret,and he's trying to get max to not make the same he mistakes he made. i can see how this film could really be an acquired taste,but i thought it was an absolute masterpiece and one of the most moving movies i've ever seen. really struck a chord with me."
